findings.claim: The attribute is not emitted for netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework targets. A context-free reviewer might call this a gap against 'all generated code', but ledger L7 records no preference there and says to follow the requirement. The change also documents the limitation in the README.

receipt_plan.detail: [L7] Generated code on netstandard2.0/.NET Framework: no preference, follow the requirement. The #if guard keeps those targets compiling, which satisfies the derived acceptance criterion.

findings.claim: Types with SuppressSourceGeneration=true get no formatter and so no attribute. This is deliberate and the README and a test both state it.

receipt_plan.detail: [L6] SuppressSourceGeneration=true types get no generated formatter, so there is nothing to decorate.

findings.claim: The README says all generated formatters and resolvers are decorated. The change does not decorate the generated GetFormatterHelper or nested helper types consistently across every template. The README also gives no way to opt out and describes no guard behaviour for custom defines, and the change adds no entry to the docs for users who want coverage of generated code.

receipt_plan.detail: Compare the README wording 'All generated formatters and resolvers' with the templates under Transforms/ and check that every emitted type has the attribute. The test only checks that each generated file contains at least one attribute, not that every type has one.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Unconditional, no setting: every generated formatter, resolver and helper class gets [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage], guarded by #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK. There is no opt-out property.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add an opt-out setting, for example a MessagePackGeneratorOptions/MSBuild property, defaulting to on. The templates then emit the attribute only when the option is enabled, so users who want coverage of generated code can turn it off. This needs an option plumbed through the generator and the templates.
